leads.title: Founding Full-Stack Product Engineer
leads.posting: Shipzy Technologies Private Limited is hiring for Founding Full-Stack Product Engineer About the Company Shipzy Technologies Private Limited is building logistics infrastructure for on-demand and last-mile delivery. The company operates across delivery operations, rider networks, fleet infrastructure and technology, with a focus on converting operational complexity into scalable products and systems. Responsibilities Work closely with the founders and operations teams to turn ambiguous business needs into reliable products. Build and improve the web platform, responsive user experiences and internal operations dashboard. Develop rider databases, onboarding workflows, order management, tracking, payout and billing systems. Create MIS and operational dashboards, automate repetitive processes and integrate third-party APIs. Contribute to the future roadmap, including rider applications, client dashboards, allocation systems, logistics APIs and notification workflows. Own the complete product lifecycle from problem discovery and architecture through deployment, debugging and iteration. Requirements 2–5 years of professional software development experience, with strong full-stack engineering fundamentals. Practical experience with frontend and backend development, databases, APIs, Git and cloud platforms. Exposure to technologies such as React or Next.js, Node.js or Python, PostgreSQL or SQL, REST APIs, AWS, GCP, Vercel, Supabase or mobile frameworks is valuable. Ability to make pragmatic technology decisions, build independently and avoid unnecessary over-engineering. Strong ownership, debugging ability and comfort working in an early-stage, fast-moving environment. Experience in logistics, mobility, SaaS, marketplaces, fleet management or other operational businesses is a plus. This is a high-ownership 0-to-1 opportunity for a builder who wants to shape technology strategy and directly influence how a logistics business operates and scales.

leads.title: Database Support Engineer (AMER)
leads.posting: Level: Entry-Level, Junior. About Supabase Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. About the Role We’re looking for an experienced Database Support Engineer to join our Support Team and help developers unblock complex issues, build more reliably, and get the most out of the Supabase platform. You’ll work closely with customers and engineering, helping us improve product quality and developer experience based on real-world usage. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions. What You’ll Be Responsible For In this role, you’ll: Investigate and resolve advanced customer issues across Postgres, Auth, RLS, Storage, Realtime, Edge Functions, and client libraries. Provide consultative, proactive advice to optimize workloads, avoid common pitfalls, and offer tailored advice to our most advanced users. Reproduce bugs , isolate root causes, propose workarounds, and escalate to engineering with solid reproduction steps. Ask smart, targeted questions that turn incomplete reports into actionable cases. Communicate clearly and empathetically with users of all levels—especially during high-impact or time-sensitive situations. Spot patterns across tickets and recommend improvements to documentation, tooling, and the product itself. Mentor junior team members and help raise the overall bar for support quality. You Might Be a Good Fit If Experience: You have 7+ years in technical support, databases, backend engineering, SRE, or a similar field. Postgres Expertise: You know PostgreSQL deeply—autovacuum behavior, WAL growth, long-running transactions, table bloat, and other internals. Performance: You’re strong in high-performance SQL and query optimization. Troubleshooting: You’re comfortable troubleshooting complex setups, including multi-tenant schema patterns. Distributed Systems: You can debug edge functions and understand distributed system behavior when failures get tricky. Data Integrity: You’ve handled data migration issues (pg_dump/restore, schema drift, failed migrations) and know how to recover safely. About | Sticker Mule Skip to main content About Sticker Mule How a late night conversation in Amsterdam, NY turned into the world's most innovative printing company that created thousands of jobs and became a globally beloved brand. Our story Shortly before Christmas in 2009, a 72-year old Tom Cummings bought his first computer and asked his friend Anthony Constantino for help using it to bet on horse racing. Tom is a skilled thoroughbred handicapper and heard he could get better horse statistics online. Instead of talking about horse racing, Constantino shared his vision with Tom for bringing manufacturing onto the Internet. Tom asked, "what do people even do on the Internet?" and Constantino responded by showing him a few web sites. The septuagenarian said "that's interesting," closed his first laptop, went home, and surprised Constantino when he visited his office the following morning with a notepad of plans for the two of them to start an Internet manufacturing company together. "What do people even do on the Internet?" Tom Cummings, co-founder, 2009 3 months later, Sticker Mule was born. Neither Tom nor Anthony had plans to sell stickers, all they wanted to do was build a modern manufacturing company that had a close connection with customers to align the success of the business with the performance of the factory floor. Of course, the two had never done anything on the Internet before so they did what anyone would do when trying to learn how to do something new. They looked up experts, found one that had a phone number and made a phone call. "We want your help to build an Internet company," the two informed Software CEO, Sean Schofield, who accepted the call and was well respected for being the creator of a prestigious open-source ecommerce platform called Spree . Schofield asked what they wanted to sell, but they hadn't decided on a product yet nor did they have a budget in mind. The confused Spree CEO tried to end the call but Anthony interjected, "well we have $100,000 to build a site" which provoked an invitation to get started. Constantino designed his concept for an online ordering process for a manufacturing company but still hadn't decided on a product when he first met his new software development team that accepted the $100,000 project. "We can get started immediately if you pick a product," Schofield insisted at their meeting. Constantino went home, talked to his brother Nicholas who also joined to help the project, and the two settled on stickers after combining various iterations of animal plus product. Print Bear, Button Frog, Magnet Duck, Gorilla Bags, were abandoned options. The trio grabbed another friend and pitched the idea to a local designer, Dave Traver , to design the web site. Dave responded, "I never designed a web site but always wanted to try." Days later, Dave had the initial design for Sticker Mule which looks much the same as it does today. Good design is long lasting they say. Within 3 months Sticker Mule launched and, to his credit, Spree's CEO, Sean Schofield, only charged $50,000 of the offered $100,000 budget. About Us - Channel3 Log in Menu Sign up About Channel3 Our vision Building the infrastructure that makes AI shopping possible. For the last thirty years, shopping has been built around a simple assumption: a person is sitting in front of a screen, typing into a search bar, opening tabs, comparing products, reading reviews, and eventually deciding what to buy. Every retailer, marketplace, and brand has optimized for that behavior because that's how the internet worked. It won't work like that for much longer. Increasingly, shopping begins with a conversation. Soon, it will end there too. People will tell AI what they need, and it will search, compare, and shop on their behalf. The internet contains billions of products, but almost none of them are described in a way machines can reliably understand. Catalogs are fragmented, specifications are inconsistent, prices change constantly, and the same product can appear differently across every retailer that sells it. Channel3 solves this problem. We bring together catalogs from thousands of brands, structure them into a common language, enrich what's missing, and keep them continuously up to date. Today that includes more than 100 million products from over 25,000 brands. It's the foundation that lets anyone build shopping experiences where AI can answer with confidence.
